q7.answer: The fanout_outbox row is inserted in the same Message Store transaction as the message, so an acknowledged message always has durable fan-out work recorded. Fan-out Workers poll the outbox and pick it up whatever happened to the gateway that did the write.

q8.answer: The record lives in the Presence Registry as user_id -> (gateway, conn_id), soft state with a 30 s TTL that each heartbeat refreshes. If the connection dies without a clean disconnect, the TTL expires 30 s after the last heartbeat and that removes the entry. A gateway whose 5 s ack timer fires also removes the entry, but only if it still names that conn_id.

q9.answer: After the inbox entry commits, the worker looks up presence and makes a deliver RPC to the named gateway (Gateway B) with the conn_id. Gateway B writes the message to the socket and starts a 5 s in-memory ack timer. The client's ack(msg_id) back to Gateway B confirms arrival, and Gateway B then marks the Offline Inbox entry delivered.

q10.answer: The record is the Offline Inbox, keyed by user_id and ordered by (conv_id, seq). The fan-out worker writes an entry for every recipient, online or not, at step 7, before it looks up presence. A client ack turns the entry into a 'delivered' tombstone, which is removed 24 h later. An entry that is never acked expires 30 days after commit.

q11.answer: Once presence has been registered (R2), the gateway reads the user's undelivered Offline Inbox entries ordered by (conv_id, seq) (R3). It then fetches the message bodies from the Message Store by (conv_id, seq) (R4) and streams them in seq order within each conversation.

q12.answer: The outbox row is marked done only after steps 7-9 have been issued, so it stays pending. When the crashed worker's 15 s shard lease expires, another worker claims the shard and redoes the row for all recipients. Insert-if-absent and tombstones stop duplicate or revived entries, the push_attempted flag keeps push at most once, and clients drop repeated live messages by msg_id.
